content.text:
This confirms the line existed before `b12a8a63` and was removed by it.

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: b12a8a63db38dcdb3b93503fe9f3552bc341a87d

## Reasoning

**(1) Investigation:** The fix (`f5c417c7`) re-adds a single line, `workflow.getSerializer().setClassloader(classLoader);`, to `CrossflowHandler.java`. I traced the full history of that line via `git log -p --follow` on the file. The line was originally introduced in commit `1849376f` (together with the `Serializer` class and its `setClassloader` method), and remained present through many subsequent commits (e.g. `4b6e50af`). It then disappears in commit `b12a8a63`, and stays missing all the way up to the fix commit `f5c417c7`.

**(2) Specific change:** `b12a8a63` is a full-file reformat/refactor of `CrossflowHandler.java`. As part of it, the author changed how the dynamically-loaded `Workflow` subclass was instantiated — switching from `getConstructor(Mode.class).newInstance(mode)` + a separate `workflow.getSerializer().setClassloader(classLoader)` call, to `getConstructor(Mode.class, ClassLoader.class).newInstance(mode, classLoader)`, presumably intending the classloader to be wired into the serializer inside the constructor instead. I verified that the generated `Workflow` subclasses (via `workflow2class.egl`) only ever expose `(Mode)` and `(Mode, int)` constructors — never `(Mode, ClassLoader)` — so this refactor was based on a constructor signature that doesn't exist, and it dropped the only code path that actually configured the serializer's classloader.

Two days later, `a6b23429` reverted the broken constructor call back to `getConstructor(Mode.class).newInstance(mode)` (fixing the immediate `NoSuchMethodException`), but did not restore the `setClassloader` call that `b12a8a63` had removed — leaving the serializer's classloader unset (defaulting to the thread context classloader, which can't resolve classes from the dynamically loaded experiment jar). This is precisely the state `f5c417c7` fixes by re-adding the line.

**(3) Evidence:** `git show b12a8a63^:...CrossflowHandler.java` confirms the line was present immediately before that commit; the diff of `b12a8a63` shows it being dropped as part of the constructor-signature change; `a6b23429`'s diff shows only the constructor call being reverted, with no mention of `setClassloader`; and `f5c417c7`'s diff re-adds exactly that missing line.

I'm confident `b12a8a63` is where the regression was introduced, since that is the sole commit that deleted the `setClassloader` call. `a6b23429` is a related follow-up fix for a different symptom (the bogus constructor signature) but did not reintroduce or fix the classloader issue, so I don't classify it as bug-introducing.
